definitions: Pattern that groups related changes into one transactional unit.
examples: Committing several repository writes as one transaction.

definitions: An operation that produces the same result no matter how many times it is applied.
examples: Retrying a PUT request is safe because it is idempotent.

definitions: A distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance at once.
examples: Choosing AP over CP during a network partition.

definitions: The four guarantees a database transaction makes so the data stays correct even if something fails partway through.
examples: A bank transfer either moves the full amount or none of it.

definitions: Splitting the model that handles writes from the model that handles reads, instead of using one model for both.
examples: Writes go through a normalized write model; reads come from a denormalized view built for the query.

expansion: stop calling a failing service for a while
definitions: A guard that stops calling a failing downstream service for a while, instead of retrying into an outage.
examples: After enough failed calls, requests to a dead payment API fail fast instead of timing out one by one.

expansion: slow consumer signals a fast producer to slow down
definitions: A way for a slow consumer to signal a fast producer to slow down, so the gap between them doesn't grow without bound.
examples: A queue that stops accepting new messages once it's full, until the consumer catches up.

expansion: replicas converge to the same value given no new writes
definitions: A consistency model where replicas are allowed to disagree temporarily, but will converge to the same value given no new writes.
examples: A DNS change takes time to propagate; different resolvers see the old and new value for a while.

expansion: local transactions with compensating actions to undo them
definitions: A way to keep data consistent across multiple services by running a sequence of local transactions, each with a compensating action to undo it if a later step fails.
examples: An order saga reserves inventory, then charges the card; if the charge fails, it releases the reserved inventory.

expansion: isolate resources per dependency so one can't exhaust them all
definitions: Isolating resources (thread pools, connections) per dependency so one failing dependency can't exhaust resources needed by the rest of the system.
examples: Giving the slow reporting API its own connection pool so it can't starve the checkout flow's connections.
